title: A to Z of financial terms | FCA
text: See our definitions to help you understand financial and legal terms. First published: 20/03/2023 Last updated: 20/03/2023 This is a new service and we are still building our library of terms - please let us know any comments or suggestions for new definitions in the page feedback section below. Disclaimer Financial services sometimes use jargon or technical terms. The definitions in the A-Z are to explain these terms in more detail. They do not replace definitions used in any statutory or regulatory context such as the FCA Handbook. We try to ensure that the definitions are correct, but we don’t give any express or implied warranty as to their accuracy. We do not accept liability for any error or omission. The definitions in the A-Z are not intended to be financial or legal advice or formal guidance, or represent a formal FCA view. We may update the definitions from time to time. Please see the FCA disclaimer . Abridged advice Account Information Service Provider (AISP) Agent Annuity Appointed representatives Authorised Authorised push payment (APP) fraud Abridged advice If you're taking advice about transferring your defined benefit (DB) pension to a defined contribution (DC) pension, advisers can offer you a short form of advice, known as abridged advice, to confirm that you are not suited to a transfer. Find out more about what this means . Account Information Service Provider (AISP) An account information service provider (AISP) lets you see all your account information from different bank accounts in one place and can analyse your spending. Providers may include budgeting apps or price comparison websites that offer product recommendations. Read more about AISPs . Agent Carries out regulated activities on behalf of another firm, known as the principal . For example, a mortgage firm (the principal) may appoint a mortgage adviser as an agent. The principal then agrees what activities an agent can do and is responsible for the conduct of that individual (see also tied agent ). Annuity An annuity is a regular income paid to you for life when you retire. You can buy an annuity using money you've saved in your pension. The annuity rate decides how much money you get each year. If you have a guaranteed annuity rate, it means the amount was fixed in your pension policy when you first signed up. Find out more about annuities and guaranteed annuity rates from MoneyHelper. Appointed representatives Some firms on the Financial Services Register are listed as 'Appointed Representatives' (ARs). This means they are carrying out activities on behalf of another firm, known as their 'principal'. The principal agrees what activities the AR can do and is responsible for that business. ARs can have more than one principal. Authorised In the UK, almost all financial firms must be authorised by us. Being ‘authorised’ means that firms must meet certain standards and follow our rules. Authorised push payment (APP) fraud A type of scam where a fraudster tricks someone into making a payment from their personal account into an account controlled by the fraudster. The account owner authorises the payment, albeit under false pretences. Read how to protect yourself from scams .
